flawed_step: To prove the statement you would need a step showing that the stable 2-WL colouring of ordered pairs determines the graph up to isomorphism, meaning that equal stable colour multisets force an isomorphism. That step cannot be justified. On a strongly regular graph srg(n,k,λ,μ), the starting colouring has three classes: diagonal, edge and non-edge. That colouring is already stable. For any pair (u,v), the multiset of (c(u,w), c(w,v)) over all w depends only on the class of (u,v) and on n, k, λ, μ. So any two strongly regular graphs with the same parameters get exactly the same stable colour multisets.
counterexample: The 4x4 rook's graph (K4□K4) and the Shrikhande graph. Both are srg(16,6,2,2). They are not isomorphic: in the rook's graph each vertex's neighbours form two disjoint triangles, while in the Shrikhande graph they form a 6-cycle. In both graphs the starting 3-class colouring is stable, with 16 diagonal pairs, 96 ordered edge pairs and 144 ordered non-edge pairs. So 2-WL does not tell them apart.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. 2-WL gives the same stable colouring to any two strongly regular graphs with the same parameters, because the counts used in each refinement step depend only on those parameters. Two such graphs that are not isomorphic are the 4x4 rook's graph and the Shrikhande graph, both srg(16,6,2,2), so 2-WL does not distinguish every pair of non-isomorphic graphs.
